name: Kids wear, toys and baby stores

problems.words: Kids outgrow sizes so fast our age-size stock never matches demand
quick_ideas: Pull sales by age band for last season once, so buying follows the ages that actually sell
Note age sizes asked for but missing for a week, so you see what you're losing.

workzap_build.text: an age-size stock grid across stores and online, with sell-through by age band and alerts when a band runs low.

problems.free_stops: How age bands are tracked and reorder alerts set is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark every missing age size asked for at the counter this week, so buying reflects what parents wanted today.
Give one staff member the job of updating one notebook of missing sizes daily, so reordering follows a single record.

problems.words: Formula and baby food near expiry, we only notice when a mother complains
quick_ideas: Check every consumable's expiry once and pull anything close to date, so nothing reaches a customer
Write expiry dates on the receiving note from now on, so the next check is quicker.

workzap_build.text: an expiry and batch register for consumables captured at receiving, with alerts and a near-expiry action list.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many consumable items do you carry?
problems.free_stops: How batches are captured and alert timings set are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the consumables shelf once this week and note which lines are closest to expiry, so staff spot trouble before complaints.
Give one person a fixed weekly shelf check for dated items, so near expiry stock gets noticed during routine.

problems.words: We had a recall and couldn't find who bought the item
quick_ideas: List which gear and electronic toys carry batch or serial numbers, so you know what could be recalled
Start noting batch numbers on sales of those items, so a lookup is possible next time.

workzap_build.text: batch and serial capture for gear and electronic toys linked to each sale, so a recall lookup shows which sales are affected.

problems.ask_first: Do you sell prams, car seats or battery toys?
problems.free_stops: How batches are linked to sales and searched is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check which recalled items still have batch details on shelf or in store records, so you know how far tracing can go.
Keep one notebook beside the till for batch noted sales of recall prone items, so lookups are possible later.

problems.words: Parents ask on WhatsApp if we have a size and we reply hours later
quick_ideas: Count unanswered stock questions for a few days, so you see how many sales wait
Give one person the WhatsApp during busy hours, so replies don't depend on whoever is free.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp stock-check flow where staff reply from a live stock lookup and the question becomes an order.

problems.ask_first: How many WhatsApp queries a day?
problems.free_stops: How the stock lookup and reply flow work is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare reply times for size questions across one busy day and one quiet day, so you see when chats start slipping.
Hand one person the phone for stock questions during the busiest shop period, so parents get quicker size answers.

problems.words: No idea who our repeat buyers are for diapers and formula
quick_ideas: Ask regulars at checkout if they'd like a reminder when their usual pack is due, with their permission, so you start a list honestly
Note which consumables people buy on a cycle, so reminders are useful.

workzap_build.text: an opt-in customer list with purchase intervals and WhatsApp reminders when a repeat buy is likely due.

problems.ask_first: Do you already keep any customer list?
problems.free_stops: How intervals are worked out and reminders timed is in the solution document.

problems.words: Birthday hamper orders get mixed up or delivered late
quick_ideas: Put all open hamper orders on one list with event date and contents, so nothing relies on memory
Confirm contents with the buyer a day before packing.

workzap_build.text: a hamper and birthday order tracker with contents, delivery slot and status.

problems.ask_first: How many hamper orders in a busy week?
problems.free_stops: The order stages and confirmation steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare hamper promise dates with actual handover dates from recent orders, so you see where lateness starts.
Put one staff member in charge of one hamper order list checked each afternoon, so custom orders stop getting mixed up.

problems.words: Toy imports stuck before Eid or Christmas
quick_ideas: List each consignment with its expected arrival against the season date, so you see which are at risk
Mark which lines arrived late, so next season those are ordered earlier.

workzap_build.text: an import tracker by consignment with expected arrival against season deadlines and alerts when one slips.

problems.ask_first: Where do most toys come from?
problems.free_stops: How shipments are tracked and flagged is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which seasonal toy lines arrived after the selling rush last time, so ordering can focus on the risky lines.
Give one person one notebook for shipment arrivals and expected dates, so late consignments are chased from one place.

problems.words: School uniform orders all come in two weeks
quick_ideas: Ask schools for expected class sizes early, so stitching starts before the rush
Stitch a stock of the most common sizes ahead, so the rush is only top-ups.

workzap_build.text: a uniform order board with sizes per class, production status, delivery and school payments tracked.

problems.ask_first: How many schools do you supply?
problems.free_stops: How orders are planned per class and tracked to payment is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count uniform orders by size and promised date for one week, so you see which days and sizes create the crush.
Give one person the job of writing every uniform order into one notebook the same day, so cutting follows one queue.

problems.words: We don't know margin by category
quick_ideas: Work out margin on your top items in each category once, so you know which category carries the shop
Use today's exchange rate for imported toys, so old purchase prices don't flatter the margin.

workzap_build.text: a category margin view (clothing, toys, consumables, gear) with landed cost kept current.

problems.ask_first: Which category do you think earns most?
problems.free_stops: How landed cost and margin are calculated is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note buying cost beside selling price for a few fast moving lines in each category, so weaker categories stop hiding behind busy sales.
Give one person one page per category for cost and selling price notes, so price checks use one shared record.

never_say: Anything on infant feeding, formula choice or child health.
Toy or car-seat safety standards or certification advice.
How to sell recalled, expired or counterfeit products.
To use children's photos or collect children's details; any injury goes to medical or emergency help first.
Anything on customs for toy imports.

sample_reply.person: A customer found an expired formula tin on our shelf last week. How do we stop this happening again?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there are practical first steps, and the first steps are simple.
First, check every consumable's expiry once this week and pull anything close to date, so nothing reaches a customer.
Second, write expiry dates on the receiving note from now on, so future checks take minutes.
What Workzap would add is: an expiry register filled at receiving, with alerts before items near their date and a list of what to pull.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
